                                  15   against Defendant Capital One Financial Corporation (“Defendant”). Plaintiffs, who are current

                                  16   customers or credit card applicants of Defendant, allege that Defendant unlawfully disclosed

                                  17   Plaintiffs’ personal and financial information to third and fourth parties.

                                  18          Before the Court is Defendant’s motion to dismiss. Having considered the parties’ briefs,

                                  19   oral arguments, the relevant legal authority, and for the reasons below, the Court GRANTS-IN-

                                  21     I.   BACKGROUND
                                  22          Defendant is a financial institution that provides financial services across the United States

                                  23   and internationally. ECF 1, (Complaint, “Compl.”) ¶ 2. To provide its services, Defendant used a

                                  24   website that allowed customers to access their account, financial services, and apply for “financial

                                  25   products like credit cards.” Id. Defendant’s website allegedly contained “invisible Third Party

                                  26   online tracking technologies” that “instantaneously and surreptitiously duplicate[d]

                                  27   communications with that webpage and sen[t] them to the Third Party.” Id. ¶ 42. These

                                  28   communications included Plaintiffs’ and Class Members’ (1) employment information; (2) bank
                                         Case 3:24-cv-05985-TLT           Document 59           Filed 03/03/25     Page 2 of 25




                                   1   account information; (3) citizenship and dual citizenship status; (4) credit card preapproval and

                                   2   eligibility; (5) credit card approval and eligibility; (6) existing user, or Customer, status; (7)

                                   3   browsing activities, including viewed pages and content; (8) credit card application status; and (9)

                                   4   other information collected through an internet “cookie.” Id. ¶ 187. Defendant used this

                                   5   information for third and fourth parties’ marketing and sales. Id. ¶ 47.

                                   6           The trackers on Defendant’s website came from Google, Microsoft, DoubleClick, New

                                   7   Relic, Adobe, Everest, Skai/Kenshoo, Snowplow, Biocatch, Tealium, and Facebook/Meta Pixel.

                                   8   Id. ¶ 51. Facebook, for instance, tracked users and the type of actions they took on Defendant’s

                                   9   website and used this information to “find new customers, drive sales, and understand ad impact.”

                                  10   Id. ¶ 48. When a customer used the Defendant’s website, Facebook would get an event informing

                                  11   it about the user’s activity. Id. ¶ 68. Defendant’s website transmitted to Facebook the specific

                                  12   page viewed by the customer, the customer’s IP address, cookies, and personal and financial
